name: Database Primary Failover
steps: Page the on-call DBA immediately via PagerDuty.
Open the #incident-response Slack channel and post initial update.
Check replication lag on replica nodes via monitoring dashboard.
If primary is unreachable, initiate automatic failover using pg_auto_failover or manual promotion.
Verify application services can connect to the new primary.
Confirm payment processing resumed by checking transaction throughput.
Post-recovery: capture WAL logs and schedule RCA within 24 hours.

name: API Service Degradation Response
steps: Acknowledge the alert in PagerDuty and open an incident bridge.
Check the API gateway metrics for error rate, latency p99, and request volume.
Determine if degradation is upstream (dependency) or local (service itself).
If upstream: notify the owning team and add to dependency health tracker.
If local: check pod health in Kubernetes, review recent deployments.
If recent deployment is suspect: trigger rollback procedure via CI/CD pipeline.
Communicate status to stakeholders via status page update.
Resolve and log actions in incident record.

name: Security Incident Response
steps: IMMEDIATELY page the Security Operations Center (SOC) on-call.
Do NOT attempt remediation without SOC authorization — evidence preservation is critical.
Isolate affected systems from network if SOC confirms active breach.
Preserve all logs: system, application, network, and access logs.
Notify CISO and Legal within 15 minutes of confirmed breach.
Activate the Security Incident Response Plan (SIRP).
Assess if PCI-DSS, HIPAA, or SOX notification obligations apply.
Do not communicate breach externally without Legal approval.
Begin chain-of-custody documentation for all forensic evidence.

name: Fraud Detection Anomaly Response
steps: Page risk-engineering on-call and fraud analyst on-call simultaneously.
Pull current fraud rate metrics from the fraud dashboard.
Determine if the anomaly is model degradation, data feed issue, or true fraud spike.
If model degradation: switch to fallback rule-based engine while model is retrained.
If data feed issue: identify the broken upstream and apply last-known-good cache.
If true fraud spike: notify compliance team and activate manual review queue.
Document all suspicious transaction IDs for forensic review.
Do not modify model thresholds without risk committee approval.

name: Data Integrity Incident Response
steps: Immediately halt batch jobs and any write-heavy processes on affected service.
Page the data engineering lead and service owner.
Run the integrity check scripts from the runbook to scope the affected records.
Identify the time window of corruption (correlate with deployments, migrations).
If financial data: notify CFO and begin regulatory impact assessment.
Do NOT attempt in-place data correction without DBA and legal sign-off.
Begin point-in-time recovery assessment — identify last clean backup.
Document every action taken with timestamps for audit trail.

name: Network Connectivity Loss Response
steps: Check network monitoring dashboard for affected segments.
Run traceroute and MTR from multiple vantage points to isolate the fault domain.
Verify DNS resolution is working correctly for affected services.
Check firewall and security group rules for recent changes.
If cloud provider issue: check provider status page and open a support ticket.
Engage network engineering on-call if fault is internal.
Test failover paths and activate secondary circuits if available.
Update status page with connectivity issue and estimated resolution.

name: General Incident Triage
steps: Acknowledge the incident and assign an incident commander.
Gather initial information: what is broken, when did it start, who is affected.
Check monitoring dashboards and recent alert history.
Identify the most likely affected service and CI.
Attempt a first-pass fix (restart, rollback, config revert).
If not resolved in 30 minutes, escalate to service owner.
Document all actions taken in the incident record.
